title: The Second Fill
subtitle: The bourbon barrel abroad
description: Why bourbon barrels are used once in Kentucky and then age most of the world's Scotch and Irish whiskey, following one barrel from the tree to its second fill. Four pours.

pours.name: Maker’s Mark
pours.notes: Nothing may be added to bourbon but water, so all of this colour came out of one new charred barrel.

pours.name: Laphroaig 10
pours.notes: Laphroaig’s ex-bourbon barrels come largely from Maker’s Mark, its sister distillery. Look under the peat smoke for the vanilla.

pours.name: Slane Irish Whiskey
pours.style: Blended Irish whiskey, three cask types
pours.notes: Brown-Forman owns Slane and Jack Daniel’s and builds its own barrels. Part of this whiskey aged in casks that held Tennessee whiskey and bourbon.

pours.name: Glenmorangie The Original 12
pours.notes: Twelve years in ex-bourbon casks, with no peat. Look for vanilla and coconut from the oak.
